{D}By a lonely prison wall, I {G}heard a young girl{D} cal{A}ling:
{D}"Michael, they are {G}taking you {A}away. {D}For you stole Travelyn‘s {G}corn,
So the {D}young might see the {A}morn. Now a prison ship lies waiting in the {D}bay.
{D}Low {G}lie {D}the fields of {h}Athenry. {D}Where once we watched the small free birds {A}fly.
{D}Our love was on the {G}wing. {D}We had dreams and songs to {A}sing. It‘s so lonely by the {A7}fields of {D}Athenry.

By a lonely prison wall, I heard a young man calling:
"Nothing matters, Mary, when you‘re free against the famine and the crown,
I rebelled, they rang me down. Now you must raise our child with dignity."

By the lonely harbour wall, she watched the last star falling,
as the prison ship sailed out against the sky sure she wait and hope and pray.
For her love in Botany Bay it‘s so lonely by the fields of Athenry.
title: The fields of Athenry
